title: Financial Controller
description:
1. Job Purpose To lead and control the companys finance, accounts, costing, commercial, purchase and stores functions. The position will ensure effective financial planning, cash-flow management, order profitability, banking arrangements, statutory compliance, audit coordination and preparation of the organisation for future investment or IPO-related activities. 
 2. Key Roles and Responsibilities 
 A. Customer PO and Sales Order Review Review customer purchase orders and sales orders before acceptance. Verify product prices, quantities, specifications, taxes, payment terms and delivery schedules. Check penalty, warranty, retention, performance guarantee and other commercial clauses. Identify financial and commercial risks and obtain necessary management approvals. Ensure customer orders are entered correctly into the ERP or accounting system. B. Sales Order Cost Verification Review pre-order costing and expected profitability of each sales order. Verify material, labour, manufacturing, galvanising, packing, transportation and overhead costs. Analyse the contribution margin and expected profit before order confirmation. Ensure deviations from approved pricing or margins are properly authorised. Coordinate with Sales, Costing, Purchase and Production departments. C. Purchase Order Verification Review vendor purchase orders before final release. Verify approved rates, quantities, specifications, taxes, delivery conditions and payment terms. Ensure vendor selection and commercial terms comply with company policies. Compare purchase prices with approved budgets and previous purchase rates. Monitor significant variations in material prices and purchase costs. D. GRN Issuance and Control Ensure timely preparation and posting of Goods Receipt Notes. Verify GRNs against purchase orders, delivery challans, invoices and actual material received. Coordinate with Stores, Purchase, Quality and Accounts for discrepancies. Monitor pending GRNs, rejected materials, shortages and excess supplies. Ensure invoices are processed only after proper GRN and quality approval. E. Cash-Flow Planning Prepare weekly, monthly and quarterly cash-flow forecasts. Plan fund requirements for salaries, vendor payments, statutory dues, operational expenses and capital expenditure. Monitor actual cash flow against forecasts and report major variances. Prioritise payments based on operational urgency and fund availability. Maintain adequate working capital for uninterrupted business operations. F. Vendor Payments and Customer Receivables Prepare and monitor vendor payment schedules. Review customer receivables and outstanding ageing reports. Coordinate with Sales and Commercial teams for collection follow-ups. Resolve invoice, payment, debit-note and credit-note disputes. Control overdue receivables and improve the companys collection cycle. Ensure vendor payments are processed according to agreed credit terms and approvals. G. Post-Order Costing and Profitability Analysis Prepare post-order costing after completion or dispatch of each order. Compare estimated costs with actual costs. Analyse material consumption, labour, production, galvanising, logistics and overhead variances. Calculate final order-wise contribution and profitability. Highlight cost overruns and recommend corrective measures. Present post-order costing reports to management. H. Banking, Negotiation and Fund Limits Manage relationships with banks and financial institutions. Negotiate working-capital limits, cash-credit limits, term loans and interest rates. Manage bank guarantees, letters of credit, bill discounting and other banking facilities. Monitor utilisation and renewal of sanctioned banking limits. Prepare financial projections and documents required by banks. Ensure timely compliance with banking conditions and covenants. Optimise finance costs and maintain sufficient liquidity. I. Audit and Statutory Compliance Coordinate statutory, internal, tax, cost, stock and banking audits. Provide accurate financial records and supporting documents to auditors. Review audit observations and ensure timely corrective actions. Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards, taxation laws and statutory requirements. Monitor GST, TDS, income tax and other statutory payments and returns. Strengthen internal financial controls and prevent financial irregularities. J. IPO Readiness and Investor Coordination Support management in assessing the companys readiness for an IPO. Coordinate with merchant bankers, auditors, legal advisers, company secretaries and consultants. Support financial due diligence and preparation of the IPO data room. Assist in financial restatement and preparation of historical financial information. Strengthen internal controls, governance systems and reporting processes. Prepare financial presentations and information required by investors. Coordinate investor meetings and respond to financial due-diligence queries. Maintain confidentiality of investor and IPO-related information. Ensure compliance with applicable SEBI, Companies Act and stock-exchange requirements in consultation with qualified advisers. K. MIS and Management Reporting Prepare monthly financial and operational MIS reports. Report revenue, profitability, cash flow, receivables, payables and banking exposure. Provide department-wise, project-wise and order-wise cost analysis. Highlight financial risks, overdue payments, cost overruns and commercial deviations. Present periodic financial performance reports to the Managing Director and Board. Support management in budgeting and strategic decision-making. L. Departmental Leadership and Coordination Lead Finance, Accounts, Costing and Commercial functions. Coordinate with Purchase and Stores for procurement and inventory controls. Define responsibilities, reporting structures and performance targets for team members. Review the performance of departmental employees. Develop effective systems, SOPs and internal controls. Ensure accuracy, confidentiality and timely completion of financial activities. 
 3. Educational Qualification Chartered Accountant (CA) preferred; or CMA/Cost Accountant, MBA Finance, M.Com or equivalent professional qualification. Additional qualification in corporate finance, taxation, banking or capital markets will be an advantage. 
 4. Experience Minimum 15 years of relevant experience , preferably in an engineering, manufacturing, fabrication or project-based organisation. At least 5 years in a senior finance leadership position . Experience in banking, working-capital management, costing, audits and statutory compliance is essential. Experience in investor due diligence, fundraising or IPO readiness will be preferred. 
 5. Key Skills and Competencies Financial planning and analysis Manufacturing and order-wise costing Cash-flow and working-capital management Banking and financial negotiations Accounts, taxation and statutory compliance Audit and internal-control management Commercial and contractual understanding Investor and IPO coordination Leadership and team management ERP and advanced MS Excel proficiency Analytical and decision-making ability High integrity and confidentiality 
 6. Key Performance Indicators Customer PO Review - Orders reviewed before acceptance and commercial risks identified. Order Costing - Accuracy of pre-order and post-order costing Profitability -Improvement in order-wise margin and reduction in cost overruns. Cash Flow Accuracy of cash-flow forecasts and availability of operational funds. Receivables - Reduction in overdue receivables and debtor days Vendor Payments - Timely payments according to agreed credit terms Banking - Timely renewal of limits and reduction in finance costs GRN Control - Timely GRN processing and reduction in pending discrepancies Audit-Timely audit completion and closure of observations Compliance-Timely statutory payments and returns without penalties MIS-Accuracy and timely submission of management reports IPO Readiness -Completion of due diligence, documentation and internal-control requirements 

 7. Authority Review and recommend sales orders, purchase orders and commercial proposals. Recommend vendor payment priorities based on cash-flow availability. Negotiate with banks and financial institutions within approved authority. Seek clarification or hold transactions with incomplete documentation. Review departmental performance and recommend corrective actions. Escalate major financial, commercial, compliance and profitability risks to management.
